evidence_note: Every entry is based on a first-to-last transcript or ASR review. Claims record what the speaker taught or reported, not independent proof of universal truth.

claims.paraphrase: Classic style treats prose as a clear window through which a reader sees a subject.
Protective throat-clearing can often be deleted without losing substantive meaning.
Turning nominalizations back into actors and verbs restores visible agency.
The curse of knowledge makes writers omit definitions, logical steps, and visible detail.
A real reader or delayed self-review exposes confusion better than imagined audience simulation.

applicability: Clarity passes for narration, exposition, lore, and reader orientation.
non_applicability: Legal precision, deliberate ambiguity, and foregrounded literary language may require different choices.
failure_boundaries: Mechanical active voice and show-don't-tell can create distortion or severe pacing drag.
counterexamples: A low-choice journey is often clearer as brief summary than as a fully dramatized scene.
ambiguities: Captioned personal names and a few inaudible moderator phrases require source verification before quotation.

claims.paraphrase: Worldbuilding and action matter more when readers care about the characters affected.
Rooting interest combines a wanted outcome, an obstacle, and personal connection to the plot.
Visible progress may occur along likeability, proactivity, competence, or a signposted mystery.
Decisions feel false when established motivation does not support them.
Distinct voice grows from background, rhetoric, and metaphor rather than catchphrases alone.

applicability: Protagonist, antagonist, supporting-cast, motivation, arc, and voice diagnosis.
non_applicability: Static iconic heroes can work without conventional positive transformation.
failure_boundaries: Scoring sliders mechanically cannot replace scene evidence and cultural context.
counterexamples: A highly competent ensemble caper can succeed without making every lead insecure or rapidly changing.
ambiguities: Examples use the lecturer's readings of well-known works and are analytical, not canonical author intent.

claims.paraphrase: An opening should establish tone, character conflict, and a mind worth following without a fixed page count.
A subplot needs its own promise, motive, and progress and should reconnect to the main story.
Strong twists enlarge or deepen conflict instead of merely canceling a prior promise.
A chapter hook works when the new fact has inferable consequence, not when a door simply opens before a cut.
Limited viewpoint cannot secretly withhold obvious knowledge without risking reader betrayal.

applicability: POV selection, opening diagnosis, subplot integration, twists, and chapter hooks.
non_applicability: Experimental second person or deliberately unstable narration needs a different contract.
failure_boundaries: Multiple POVs spend orientation and attachment; omniscience needs an intentional narrator and transition discipline.
counterexamples: Opening a door and cutting before an ordinary delivery creates interruption, not earned suspense.
ambiguities: The lecture begins with broader plot questions before the formal viewpoint section.

claims.paraphrase: A short story aims at a specific emotional punch while a novel has more room for immersion.
Milieu, inquiry, character, and event threads have distinct opening and closure conditions.
Nested story threads should normally close from the innermost thread outward.
Yes-but and no-and make attempts produce progress or worsening consequences.
An ending should mirror opening character, place, and genre mood while showing change.

applicability: Short fiction, chapter-scale story boxes, compressed openings, and thread closure.
non_applicability: Pure lyric fragments and intentionally unresolved experiments may reject goal-and-closure logic.
failure_boundaries: The MICE word-count formula is a planning heuristic, not a publication law.
counterexamples: Resolving a romance while never answering the murder question leaves the inquiry thread unpaid.
ambiguities: Several classroom fictional names and formula phrases are imperfectly captioned.

claims.paraphrase: Drafting, narrative revision, and polishing are separate passes with different decisions.
The first draft is exploratory and should be completed through small repeatable effort.
Predictive writing derives the next scene from already planted necessity and implication.
Character action and choice generate cause and effect that make the following scene necessary.
A final read-aloud lets the writer experience and repair the manuscript before external judgment.

applicability: Separating discovery drafting, structural revision, and publication polish.
non_applicability: A serial already published cannot freely reorder history without change control.
failure_boundaries: Suspending judgment does not authorize publishing an unreviewed exploratory draft.
counterexamples: Polishing every sentence before discovering the real causal story wastes effort and resists necessary cuts.
ambiguities: Some techniques are attributed orally to other books and should not be treated as original claims.

claims.paraphrase: Plot can be diagnosed as promise, progress, and payoff even in discovery writing.
When progress and opening promise mismatch, revising the opening may be cheaper than replacing the whole middle.
Promises include tone, character, series structure, and central conflict, not plot facts alone.
Mystery progress needs visible clues, exclusions, and signposts that tell readers movement is occurring.
A satisfying payoff should be surprising in form and feel inevitable after review of its preparation.

applicability: Promise ledgers, midpoint repair, multi-track progress, endings, and serialized expectation control.
non_applicability: The framework does not dictate one plot shape or require every payoff to be triumphant.
failure_boundaries: Signposting can become repetitive explanation; surprise without preparation becomes arbitrary.
counterexamples: An action sequence that changes no relationship, plan, information, or risk is event density without satisfying progress.
ambiguities: Film and novel examples represent the lecturer's critical interpretation.

claims.paraphrase: Serial platforms can deliver recurring posts to subscribers while retaining an author archive.
Episode endings benefit from a consequential hook when access to the next installment requires another decision.
Previewed first paragraphs need an immediate legible desire, disruption, or question.
Polls and author notes can gather bounded reader reaction during serialization.
Serialized material may later be edited and packaged into other book formats.

applicability: Preview-based episodic publication, subscriptions, comments, and later edition planning.
non_applicability: It does not prove current availability, payout, exclusivity, discoverability, or territorial access.
failure_boundaries: Artificial hooks, continuity-by-poll, and unverified crowd research can weaken a work.
counterexamples: Stopping in mid-action without a consequence is a payment interruption rather than a narrative hook.
ambiguities: Speaker switches and overlapping captions make exact names and historical platform terms uncertain.

claims.paraphrase: The speaker describes revising and expanding a project for years before entering web serialization.
Cover, blurb, genre, and opening jointly establish promises readers later judge.
Subscription infrastructure can automate delivery but does not itself discover readers.
The speaker separates serialized and conventional production pipelines, including editing and beta work.
Early serialized feedback can reveal slow openings and audience mismatch before a book edition is final.

applicability: Buffering, feedback-to-edition pipelines, promise testing, and separating formats.
non_applicability: Sales, pricing, platform features, and funnel conversion are dated self-reports.
failure_boundaries: Feedback quality varies and a serial test cannot prove causation or market size.
counterexamples: A platform with automation but no audience source solves delivery while leaving discovery untouched.
ambiguities: Caption overlap duplicates phrases and makes some speaker attributions uncertain.

claims.paraphrase: LitRPG makes game rules visible and operable to characters, with varying statistical density.
Discovery plotting can coexist with a strict rule and mathematics reference table.
System detail should be selected for current reader experience and medium rather than displayed by default.
Power growth retains tension through adaptive opposition, non-numeric challenges, and real failure.
Repeated grind should be compressed unless a scene adds a new rule, choice, cost, or variation.

applicability: LitRPG, explicit systems, progression fantasy, long growth arcs, and audio-friendly stat presentation.
non_applicability: Genre, market, and community observations are not universal sales forecasts.
failure_boundaries: Improvised payoff rules, long irrelevant stat blocks, and purely numeric escalation undermine trust and tension.
counterexamples: A level increase that changes no available choice is bookkeeping, not narrative progression.
ambiguities: Names and some numerical examples in automatic captions require audio verification before quotation.

claims.paraphrase: The author treats pseudonymity as professional separation, communication preference, and irreversible safety protection.
Reader preference is described as a weather vane rather than the steering wheel for ending direction.
A broad route can coexist with organic local discovery and experimentation.
Preparation, depression, boredom, and deadline exhaustion can present as different kinds of writing blockage.
A multi-day chapter pipeline uses drafting, reader or beta observation, editing, and continuity repair.

applicability: Long serial planning, feedback boundaries, privacy, team editing, and sustainable chapter cycles.
non_applicability: Exceptional word counts and revenue mix are individual outcomes, not norms.
failure_boundaries: Health concerns require professional support; a workflow must not normalize chronic overload.
counterexamples: Changing an intended ending only because readers guessed it sacrifices causality for surprise.
ambiguities: The interview uses written answers read by another person, and automatic timestamps include duplicated caption fragments.

claims.paraphrase: Long gaps between writing sessions increase loss of series details.
Immediate short notes can preserve character and plot cues without exhaustive documentation.
Recording goals and trajectory helps a writer resume with current location, direction, and actor.
A full-series outside reader can detect semantic continuity errors missed during local editing.
Continuity deserves an independent normal-speed reading pass rather than being mixed into polish.

applicability: Long series, irregular schedules, complex relationships, and continuity handoff.
non_applicability: A suggested short book cycle is not realistic or appropriate for every author or research-heavy project.
failure_boundaries: Faster production cannot replace a canonical ledger, outside review, or sustainable health limits.
counterexamples: A family relationship error survived author and beta review across ten volumes before a complete reader found it.
ambiguities: Subjective quantifiers and the closing claim that long series are better are opinions, not measured findings.

claims.paraphrase: Ongoing reading and attention to current works help a new writer calibrate expectations.
Expressive intent and commercial discipline should constrain each other.
A story goal differs from fantasies about recognition, income, or being regarded as a master.
Trend imitation can conflict with an established writing temperament and produce an incoherent hybrid.
Reader reward must be embodied in the protagonist's observable action and consequence.

applicability: Concept selection, trend pressure, reader reward, and diagnosing author-only fantasies.
non_applicability: The clip does not supply platform performance data or prove that trend following always fails.
failure_boundaries: Commercial calibration can become empty imitation; expressive freedom can become unreadable private symbolism.
counterexamples: Wanting praise for writing a prestigious-looking book gives the protagonist no actionable payoff.
ambiguities: ASR likely confuses 表达欲, 小白文, and several book titles; paraphrase rather than quote.

claims.paraphrase: A main desire needs supporting experience, loss, and a characteristic way of acting.
A single system-reward loop fatigues unless other long expectations change its meaning.
Designing the eventual settlement first helps align antagonistic pressure and emotional setup.
Humiliation creates anticipation only when readers can see a credible route to consequential response.
A climax gains force when one decisive action settles several prepared emotional promises.

applicability: Revenge, reversal, identity reveal, face-saving, and emotional climax design.
non_applicability: Not every conflict should promise triumphant retaliation, especially tragedy or moral compromise.
failure_boundaries: Pressure without a credible response path becomes prolonged misery; unrelated humiliation fragments the core.
counterexamples: Generic insults about ugliness offer no specific capability, secret, or action through which to settle the promise.
ambiguities: Book names and colloquial examples contain ASR errors and should not be cited verbatim.

claims.paraphrase: A mainline states what story this is rather than cataloging the world.
Supporting threads should wrap around the mainline to create conflict and expectation.
The protagonist's present desire is shaped by experience and emotion.
A mainline includes both the target and the characteristic behavior used to pursue it.
A clear drive can support many side problems when each changes progress, obstacle, cost, or relationship.

applicability: One-line mainline, long outline, side-thread relevance, and protagonist drive.
non_applicability: A one-line mainline does not replace volume architecture, character contradiction, or ending design.
failure_boundaries: A stated ambition without causal experience and observable action remains a slogan.
counterexamples: A reborn protagonist declaring that they will become busy has no reason, strategy, or legible story direction.
ambiguities: Automatic transcription distorts several title and proper-name examples.

claims.paraphrase: An information jump occurs when familiar words combine into meaning for which the reader lacks prerequisites.
Unfamiliar concepts become readable when rebuilt from known categories, boundaries, and functions.
Explaining invented spatial terms only through more invented spatial terms accumulates confusion.
Large techniques feel powerful after their component concepts have been established in simpler use.
World information should be introduced when an action or decision makes it necessary.

applicability: Worldbuilding, openings, new systems, spatial hierarchy, institutions, and compressed exposition.
non_applicability: The method does not require explaining common genre conventions to every expert reader.
failure_boundaries: Explaining everything creates encyclopedic drag; explaining nothing creates accumulating cognitive debt.
counterexamples: Defining one invented realm through three other undefined realms preserves every term and conveys no usable model.
ambiguities: ASR confuses several famous technique names and local terms; only the conceptual mechanism is retained.

claims.paraphrase: Dense events within one day do not by themselves define fast narrative pacing.
Fast pacing reduces ineffective information and ineffective event material.
An unrelated bridge scene interrupts momentum even when many events surround it.
A clear need and prior fact can introduce a new game phase without an information jump.
Small daily events can remain lively when they have focus, character contrast, and later connection.

applicability: Chapter pacing, transitions, memory points, quiet bridge chapters, and removal of filler.
non_applicability: Atmospheric, reflective, or deliberately disorienting work may value effects other than rapid comprehension.
failure_boundaries: Maximizing turns creates summary-like noise; formula obsession can inhibit drafting.
counterexamples: A sequence of exams, fights, and victories feels slow when an unrelated segment breaks causality and carries no memory point.
ambiguities: ASR confuses work and character names; final timestamp slightly exceeds container duration.

claims.paraphrase: Scene connection can be judged by low irrelevant material and smooth causal continuation.
Inserted setting information should serve the current scene's central emotion or decision.
Removing all transition in pursuit of speed creates broken rhythm and writing paralysis.
A sequence feels continuous when one consequence triggers the next conflict and settlement.
When no outline exists, the next unit can grow from a live thread in the current text; no possible next event is a different blockage.

applicability: Chapter-to-chapter causality, map transitions, payoff chains, and recovery from local outline gaps.
non_applicability: A local thread-bridging method cannot replace a missing series engine or complete creative block diagnosis.
failure_boundaries: Overlinear connection forbids healthy new threads; an outline can still contain unsupported character choices.
counterexamples: Moving to a new region only because the hero has maxed the old one supplies no present agent, motive, or cost.
ambiguities: ASR distorts titles, names, and a sword example; no visual diagram was reviewed.
